scored_features.gate_reasoning: G1: NIHSS is present in trial_measured_features so the feature is observed in the data. G2: The hypothesis states concrete pathophysiological steps (core vs penumbra size, sICH risk modulation by infarct size/location) linking baseline NIHSS to differential benefit from reperfusion, which is a biologically coherent mechanism. G3: The claim is that NIHSS changes the biology of treatment response (amount of salvageable tissue and hemorrhage risk) not merely baseline event-rate amplification, so this is a plausible treatment effect modifier. G4: Multiple trial analyses and pooled data (including IST-3 subgroup work and meta-analyses) have examined NIHSS bands and shown heterogeneous absolute benefits and risks across severity strata, supporting the interaction in the literature. G5: The hypothesis defines clear, operational NIHSS bands (0-4, 5-15, 16-20, >20) and conditional rules with imaging/time-to-treatment that could guide clinical decisions, so it is actionable.
scored_features.justification: All gates pass; decisive support comes from G3 (a mechanistic PD/pathophysiologic rationale that NIHSS reflects salvageable tissue and bleeding risk) which, together with published subgroup analyses (G4), makes this a credible and actionable modifier.

scored_features.gate_reasoning: G1: Age is recorded in trial_measured_features so the feature is observed in the data. G2: The hypothesis names biological/physiologic mediators (vascular fragility, frailty, comorbidity, competing mortality and sICH susceptibility) that plausibly link age to differential alteplase harm/benefit and thus is biologically coherent. G3: The claim is that advancing age changes treatment biology (higher bleeding fragility, frailty affecting recovery and competing mortality) rather than only changing baseline risk, so it can be a genuine effect modifier. G4: The interaction of age with thrombolysis has been examined in multiple trials and pooled analyses (including IST-3-era data), with consistent evidence that age influences absolute benefit/harm though relative efficacy may be preserved in selected elderly; this provides literature support. G5: The proposal gives operational strata (e.g., <65, 65-79, ≥80) and conditional modifiers (pre-stroke mRS, imaging, time), which are measurable and usable in clinical decision-making.
scored_features.justification: All gates pass; decisive reinforcement is G4 because multiple RCTs and pooled analyses have evaluated age-related heterogeneity, supporting the biologically plausible (G3) interaction and making it clinically actionable.

scored_features.gate_reasoning: G1: Weight is included in trial_measured_features so the feature is observed in the data. G2: The hypothesis articulates a concrete pharmacokinetic mechanism (mg/kg dosing with a fixed maximum dose → lower mg/kg exposure in high-weight patients leading to reduced recanalization) which is biologically coherent. G3: If dose-capping occurred, this creates a genuine PK-driven treatment effect modifier (different drug exposure leading to different efficacy/bleeding), so the mechanism is causally plausible in principle. G4: However, whether IST-3 applied a fixed cap frequently enough to cause clinically meaningful underdosing in high-weight patients is uncertain and high-quality trial evidence demonstrating a weight (or capped-dose) × alteplase efficacy interaction is limited; therefore G4 FALSE — cascade: G5 also FALSE.
scored_features.justification: Fails at G4: despite a clear PK rationale and the feature being measured (G1–G3), there is limited trial-level evidence that routine dose-capping caused clinically important heterogeneity in alteplase efficacy in IST-3, so the interaction is not supported for action; this is an underexplored (novel) hypothesis meriting further investigation.
